text:
devon: Heads-up — saw a reproducible p99 latency regression on longctx workloads after the recent paging change. Repro steps in the thread below.
maria: ugh, which change? the sweepback eviction that prioritizes compactness over recency?
akshay: yes, the sweepback commit (D4567) changed the weight from recency->compactness to try and reduce fragmentation. Seems fine for short sessions but long contexts losing big prefixes.
devon: repro: run longctx-sim with 2M tokens across mixed tenants. p50 stable, p95 similar, p99 jumped from ~110ms -> ~260ms. memory shows KV resident set climbing steadily instead of plateauing.
sylvia: can you paste the perf snapshot and the heap table? also any kernel selection differences (fp16 vs int8) that could affect cache behavior?
devon: attaching snippet of the flame + tail logs (trimmed):
```
# flame top (tokens/sec suppressed)
serving_runtime::kv::get_prefix  ────────── 48%  p99 hot
serving_runtime::kernel::matmul    ─── 6%
serving_runtime::batch::coalesce   ─── 10%
rpc::serialize                   ─── 2%
```
# mem growth
tenant A: kv_bytes  -> 1.8GB -> 2.5GB over 30m
tenant B: kv_bytes  -> 1.2GB -> 1.6GB
```
maria: that kv::get_prefix high percentage suggests repeated misses or repeated long scans. Sweepback may be collapsing different prefix keys into larger ones, forcing repeated recompute.
akshay: also noticed batching switched to conservative coalesce in the same deploy (auto-batch threshold lowered). Might be fewer requests per batch so KV reuse is less effective.
perf-bot: incident-note: linked trace http://perf/redwood/trace/176999/evict-sweepback-126
sylvia: theory: large prefix objects are sticky but canonicalization changed key shape. If cache key includes session_epoch + sanitized-prefix-hash, small differences cause duplicate entries and eviction churn.
devon: yes — saw many near-duplicate keys with only last 4 bytes different. That explains fragmentation: tiny key variance -> many small entries, then sweepback compacts them but policy incorrectly marks recent large prefixes as evictable.
maria: quick test idea: run a shadow patch that normalizes prefix hashing (truncate to 64-bit canonical) and revert sweepback aggressiveness. If p99 improves, we isolate key skew vs eviction logic.
akshay: I'll prepare the canary patch. Plan:
  1) shadow deploy to a single shard with normalized prefix hash (mask lower entropy)
  2) keep old eviction weights but increase sticky-window from 5m -> 15m
  3) collect kv-residency hist, prefix-cardinality, p99 for 2 hours
sylvia: add metrics: prefix_canonicalization_hits, duplicate-prefix-groups, avg-prefix-size, eviction_runs_per_min
devon: also add per-kernel metric to check if kernel selection change correlates: kernel_choice_by_shard (int8/float16/fp32) and batch_size_hist.
maria: command to run the local repro (devon posted):
```
$ ./tools/longctx-sim --tenants 50 --duration 1800 --seed 42 \
  --enable-kv-trace --out /tmp/kv-trace.json
```
devon: results from a quick local run (no normalization):
- p99 248ms
- unique-prefix-keys 132k -> duplicates 28k
- eviction rate 420/s with ~35% sweepback-compact steps
akshay: after applying normalization patch locally (truncated hash) quick run:
- p99 118ms
- unique-prefix-keys 48k -> duplicates 1.2k
- eviction rate 120/s
sylvia: promising. If we can get same drop in canary, we can do two small follow-ups: (A) canonicalize keys in compile path; (B) revert sweepback weight tweak and instead use an LRU-ish window for large-prefix objects.
maria: we should also confirm this doesn't worsen memory tail for workloads that previously benefited from sweepback (short sessions). Add a short-session A/B test.
devon: action items:
- akshay: roll shadow canary -> shard r12 with prefix-hash normalization + sticky-window=15m (ETA 2h)
- sylvia: add the extra metrics and a dashboard panel (ETA 4h)
- maria: run short-session regression suite on canary after 30m (ETA 3h)
- devon: coordinate rollback if p95 or p50 regress >5% or p99 not improved
akshay: will post canary URL and baseline snapshots once up. ping me if you want the live logs.
maria: thanks. one more ask — let's add a small test harness in CI to fuzz prefix key entropy so we don't regress this again.
perf-bot: perf-alert queued: if p99 > 200ms for >5min on prod shard -> auto rollback
devon: thanks team. keeping this thread as the bisect log. I'll paste canary links and final numbers here.
